config.title: React.memo

intro.title: React.memo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application with two counter components to see how React.memo optimizes performance. You'll learn how React.memo prevents unnecessary re-renders of a component when its props haven't changed. The main technologies used are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and the React.memo higher-order component. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to performance optimization in React.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, React.memo is essential for optimizing performance in complex, frequently updating UIs. For example, in a live dashboard displaying real-time financial charts and metrics, each chart component can be wrapped with React.memo to prevent unnecessary re-renders when unrelated dashboard filters change. Similarly, in a large e-commerce product listing with interactive filters (like size or color), memoizing the product card components ensures smooth user interactions by avoiding re-renders of unchanged items. This pattern is also valuable in data-heavy admin panels where tables or lists update based on user actions, helping maintain responsiveness and a seamless experience.

objectives: Apply React.memo to wrap a functional component for performance optimization
Configure memoized components to prevent unnecessary re-renders when props remain unchanged
Construct a parent component that passes props to memoized child components
Implement a comparison function to control when memoized components should update
Initialize state variables in a parent component that trigger re-renders of memoized children
Render memoized components alongside non-memoized components to observe performance differences
Manipulate prop values to demonstrate when memoized components re-render versus skip rendering

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for using React and state in a TypeScript component are added.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns JSX containing a <div> element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns a div element.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named App and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The component is missing or doesn't return a div. Try creating a function named App that returns

steps.title: Create a child component without memo
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ChildComponent that accepts a count prop and displays it.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called ChildComponent that takes props as a parameter and returns JSX showing the count value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent function is defined that receives a count prop and renders it in the UI.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined as a function or arrow function, accepts a count prop, and returns JSX containing the count value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it accepts a count prop and displays it in the returned JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named ChildComponent that takes a count prop and shows it.

steps.title: Add state to the App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, initialize a count state variable using useState, starting with a value of 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the initial value and specify the type as number.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization
const [count, setCount] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a count state variable initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState call that initializes a count variable with value 0 and type number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've properly initialized the count state with useState and specified the type as number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count state isn't properly initialized. Make sure to use useState with an initial value of 0 and specify the type as number.

steps.title: Add an increment handler
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named increment that increases the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setCount function to update the state. You can use the current state value to calculate the new count.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has an increment function that can be used to update the count state.
successCriteria: An increment function is defined inside the App component that uses setCount to increase count by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly updates the count state using setCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function is missing or doesn't properly update the count state.

steps.title: Add a button to trigger re-renders
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment Count' that calls the increment handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick attribute that references your increment handler function. The button should display text that indicates its purpose.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an interactive button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a button that, when clicked, triggers the increment handler to update the count state.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Increment Count' is added inside the App component's return statement, with an onClick handler that calls the increment function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and onClick handler to call the increment function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the required properties. Add a button with text 'Increment Count' and an onClick handler.

steps.title: Render the child component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render the ChildComponent and pass the count state as a prop named 'count'.
steps.hint: Add <ChildComponent count={count} /> inside the div, after the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: passing a prop to a child component
<ChildComponent value={someValue} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent is rendered inside App with the count state passed as a prop.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is rendered with count prop passed correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've rendered the ChildComponent, but make sure to pass the count state as a prop named 'count'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent should be rendered inside App's return statement with the count prop.

steps.title: Import React.memo
steps.instruction: Add React.memo to the existing import statement from 'react'.
steps.hint: Update the import line to include memo alongside React and useState.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement will include memo, making it available for use.
successCriteria: memo is imported from 'react' in the same statement as React and useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but ensure memo is included in the import statement from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing memo. Update it to import memo from 'react'.

steps.title: Wrap child component with React.memo
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing ChildComponent with React.memo to create a memoized version. Assign the result to a new constant named MemoizedChild.
steps.hint: Use React.memo to wrap the component. The syntax is: const MemoizedChild = React.memo(ChildComponent);
steps.analogousExample:
// Wrapping a component with React.memo
const MemoizedGreeting = React.memo(GreetingComponent);
steps.expectedOutcome: A memoized version of ChildComponent is created and assigned to MemoizedChild.
successCriteria: The result is assigned to a constant named MemoizedChild
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to wrap ChildComponent with React.memo and assign it to a constant named MemoizedChild.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for React.memo. You need to wrap ChildComponent and assign the result to MemoizedChild.

steps.title: Use the memoized component
steps.instruction: Replace the original ChildComponent with the memoized version in the App component's render output.
steps.hint: Look for where you rendered ChildComponent earlier and replace it with the memoized version you created.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now renders the memoized version of ChildComponent instead of the original.
successCriteria: MemoizedChild is used in the App component's JSX instead of ChildComponent
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the memoized component (MemoizedChild) in the App component's render output.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced ChildComponent with MemoizedChild in the App component's JSX.
